Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old female with several days of worsening central/lower abdominal pain (constant, around 8/10) accompanied by nausea and light vaginal bleeding; history of constipation last week but bowel function now normal. On Implanon contraception. Last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago. Plan includes in-clinic abdominal examination and a current pregnancy test today, with urgent review if symptoms worsen or if fluids cannot be kept down.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute lower abdominal pain
  - Onset: a few days ago; persistent and worsening.
  - Location: lower abdomen, midline below the umbilicus.
  - Symptoms: constant pain ~8/10; nausea (vomiting not established); no fever; bowel habit: constipation last week, currently normal; no noted urinary symptoms.
  - ROS: no shortness of breath; no significant systemic symptoms documented.
  - Social/Medications/Examination: Lives with husband and husband’s family; works as a school teacher; on Implanon contraception; amoxicillin allergy.
  - Specialist/allied health/differential: not specified.

Issue 2:
- Gynecologic symptoms with possible pregnancy consideration
  - Onset/timeline: light vaginal bleeding described; last period ~2–3 weeks ago; regular menses with Implanon but bleeding described as light pink; recent sexual activity; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago.
  - Symptoms: light vaginal bleeding/discharge; light pink color; intermittent vaginal discharge; no heavy bleeding reported.
  - ROS: associated nausea; no fever; otherwise asymptomatic.
  - Medications/history: Implanon contraception in place; amoxicillin allergy; no prior pregnancies.
  - Social history: sexual activity ongoing; travels abroad >1 year ago.
  - Plan/differential: pregnancy test today recommended; if positive, urgent/straightaway evaluation indicated.

Issue 3:
- Allergies and contraception history
  - Allergy: Amoxicillin allergy.
  - Contraception: Implanon (implant) in place; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Medications:
- Implanon (contraceptive implant) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin allergy.

Past Medical History:
- Amoxicillin allergy.
- No prior pregnancies reported.

Social History:
- Living: lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Occupation: school teacher.
- Travel: abroad about a year ago.
- Smoking: not documented; patient unsure about smoking status.
- Alcohol: reports drinking a lot; exact amount not documented.
- Drugs: none reported.
- Sexual activity: regular; contraception with Implanon.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vital signs: not provided.
- Exam findings: not performed yet; plan to arrange a face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic.

Plan:
- Arrange a face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic via the support line.
- Perform pregnancy test today; if positive, patient should be seen urgently.
- Advise patient to seek urgent care if pain worsens or if she cannot tolerate oral intake or fluids.
- If symptoms worsen or new red-flag features arise, contact support/return for earlier evaluation.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals (no vitals documented); results of any physical abdominal exam (not yet performed); imaging or labs beyond pregnancy test not available; preventive health measures (cervical screening, mammography, vaccines) not documented.
- Internal conflicts: none explicit in transcript; some garbled phrasing around travel history (“out in the air”) and ambiguous smoking status.
- Transcript quality: some inaudible/garbled portions; overall clinical details are captured as stated, with appropriate caution about uncertainties.

Document quality note:
- If any element is later clarified (e.g., exact timing of bleeding, imaging results, pregnancy test result), update the Problem List accordingly.
